newsitem.title: UK: UK MPs demand more government money for tourism.
newsitem.headline: UK MPs demand more government money for tourism.

text.p: UK parliament's National Heritage Committee called on Wednesday for the government to pump more money into the promotion of British tourism.
Britian attracts about 24 million overseas visitors, bringing in 12.1 billion stg, yet funding for the British Tourist Authority is just 35.5 million stg a year.

The all-party panel of MPs said it would be a worthwhile investment to increase its financial support for the BTA over the next five years by 100 million stg, with the bulk of it targeted on the United States, Europe and the Far East.
The committee also called for a complete reappraisal of funding to the English Tourist Board, whose grant-in-aid from the government in 1996-97 is just 10 million stg.
"It is ludicrous and unacceptable that England's tourist attractions should be undersold in this way," the MPs said.
The panel also recommended that the way the government supports the industry should be urgently re-examined, criticising a lack of proper coordination.
"Although it is given a good deal of attention by government, it (tourism) does not receive enough financial support," the report said.

"It employs more people than argiculture, coal mining, steel making, automobile manufacture, aircraft manufacture, food production and the textile industry put together. Yet it is insignificantly recognised as the central element in the economy that it is." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
